outcome: The general Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture (an exponential-in-k bound C(r)^k for every fixed r>2) remains open, but two genuine restricted cases were settled and published in the window: Balogh, Bernshteyn, Delcourt, Ferber and Pham (arXiv:2408.04165, Aug 2024; Combinatorica 2025) proved a near-conjectural bound for families of bounded VC-dimension, obtaining a sharp (r-1)^k bound in the VC-dimension-1 case, and improved the general bounded-VC-dimension case beyond earlier work of Fox–Pach–Suk. A September 2026 preprint by Ge, Wang, Xu and Zhao (arXiv:2609.18995) claims to fully resolve the conjecture for all families of bounded VC-dimension. A June 2026 preprint by Mishra (arXiv:2606.02667) claims the conjecture for shifted families. All are restrictions to special classes of families, not resolutions of the stated conjecture, which is still open even for r=3 in general.

disputes.summary: Junichiro Fukuyama has repeatedly claimed (arXiv:2212.13609, first posted Dec 2022, predating the window, with revised versions posted through June 2026 to 'fix the error' of the previous version) to have a full proof of the general Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture. He runs a personal blog (sites.psu.edu/sunflowerconjecture) documenting ongoing work and self-identified errors. No journal acceptance, no expert digestion (e.g. no discussion found on Gil Kalai's blog, which actively covers sunflower-conjecture developments, nor on MathOverflow), and the author's own site shows him shifting to related side-topics rather than declaring the proof stable as of September 2026. A related Fukuyama preprint (arXiv:2510.19037, Oct 2025) claims a 'sub-logarithmic base' bound but is also a restricted/incremental claim, not a verified full resolution.

summary: The sunflower conjecture as stated (an exponential bound C(r)^k, C depending only on r, for every fixed r>2) is still open in general as of September 2026; the best fully general bound remains the Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang breakthrough (2019, predating the window) as refined by Bell–Chueluecha–Warnke to O(r log k)^k, still carrying a log k factor rather than the pure constant the conjecture requires, so no fully general progress happened inside the window. Within the window, genuine restricted cases were settled: Balogh, Bernshteyn, Delcourt, Ferber and Pham (arXiv:2408.04165, posted 8 Aug 2024, journal-published in Combinatorica 45 (2025)) proved the conjecture-strength bound for families of bounded VC-dimension d, with a sharp (r-1)^k bound for the d=1 case, improving on Fox–Pach–Suk; this is a peer-reviewed, well-authored result restricting the ambient family class (a case, per §3.1, since it removes territory — VC-dimension-bounded families — from the general open problem) and is coded `partial`/`confirmed`. Two further 2026 preprints extend this line: Ge–Wang–Xu–Zhao (arXiv:2609.18995, first version dated 17 Jul 2026 per the paper header though the arXiv ID implies a September posting — a discrepancy I flag but did not resolve) claim the full bounded-VC-dimension case, and Mishra (arXiv:2606.02667) claims the shifted-families case; neither preprint appears yet to have expert digestion, so they support the `partial` classification but do not move the record to `resolved`. None of these results, nor the still-unverified and self-corrected Fukuyama preprints claiming a full proof, involve any AI system — all are traditional combinatorial arguments (compression/shifting methods, VC-dimension/entropy techniques), and none of the papers or surrounding commentary mention AI, machine learning, or automated theorem-proving tools. I treat the Fukuyama claims (in `disputes`) as not evidencing a change to `status` because they lack any expert acceptance and have a documented, self-acknowledged history of errors spanning nearly four years.
competing_reading: One could argue the VC-dimension and shifted-family results are 'related problems' (variants changing the ambient family class) rather than 'cases' of the stated conjecture, since the Wikipedia bullet is phrased as an unrestricted statement about all k-uniform families. I read them as cases because bounded-VC-dimension families and shifted families are subsets of the families the general conjecture quantifies over — restricting the domain removes territory from the open problem rather than changing the question — consistent with the triage's judgment. If one instead reads 'the sunflower conjecture' as inherently meaning only the fully general, unrestricted statement such that any added hypothesis makes it a different problem, the status would be `open` with `no_change_found` true.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (accepted by experts) of the general C(r)^k bound with no additional hypothesis on the family, or an expert digestion (blog post, journal referee report, or citation as settled) of Fukuyama's claim, or expert commentary situating the VC-dimension/shifted-family results explicitly as 'cases' versus 'variants' of the Wikipedia-stated conjecture.

events.credibility_reason: Landmark problem; nearly four years with no expert uptake (none on Kalai's blog, which covers the topic, or MathOverflow); many patch revisions to 'fix the error' of the previous version; later same-topic work (Balogh et al., Ge et al.) treats the general conjecture as open. Also pre-snapshot, so could not set the status in any case.

judgement.doubts: Bounded-VC-dimension and shifted families are subclasses of the families the bullet quantifies over, so these are cases, not variants. Fukuyama's 2025 bound, even if correct, is progress tier and below partial. The Ge et al. date discrepancy (header 17 Jul 2026 vs 2609 ID) does not affect the status.
